reason: This text (Ezekiel 37:1-14, the dry bones vision) explicitly demonstrates the opposite of the statement. God promises restoration and redemption of Israel, repeatedly identifying them as 'My people' (עַמִּי) and committing to bring them back from their graves to their land. The passage affirms God's loyalty through promises of resurrection and renewal, not abandonment or replacement. God's message to Israel through the prophet is one of covenantal faithfulness and restoration, directly contradicting any suggestion that God considers replacing them with another people.
